key_insight: A density-based topology optimization framework can directly include multidirectional mutual radiation by coupling ray-traced radiative exchange with finite-element conduction analysis.
engineering_relevance: This enables more realistic design of lightweight thermal-management structures for space electronics, such as radiative heat sinks and radiation shields.
method: Integrates a zonal-method radiation solver with ray tracing into finite-element heat conduction.
Treats intermediate density regions as participating media during optimization for physically consistent radiation evaluation.
Uses adjoint-based analytical sensitivities and verifies them against finite-difference results.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical examples on radiative heat sinks and radiation shields, with sensitivity accuracy confirmed by comparison to finite-difference calculations.
watch_item: Ray-tracing-based radiation analysis inside each optimization step may increase computational cost and implementation complexity.
paper_title: Topology optimization of conduction-radiation problems based on a ray-tracing approach
